claim: Humans: metacognition correlates with performance (math r=.37 [.29,.44], 29 studies; general r=.20 to .23 offline), and online measures give larger links than questionnaires (r=.54 vs .30; .53 vs .23). All correlational.
agent_test: none: human correlate only; use as prior for what to log online during a run
audit_note: Muncer (Springer OA): 74 effect sizes, 29 studies, r=.37 [.29,.44]; online .54 (k=14) vs offline .30 (k=60), p=.034; Ohtani&Hisasaka online .53 vs offline .23. Slip: Dent&Koenka's .20 is their overall r (their offline is .15), so 'general r=.20 to .23 offline' is loose.

claim: Meta-analyses find that metacognition measured during the task (think-aloud, behaviour observation) correlates more strongly with performance than after-the-fact questionnaires (math r=.54 vs .30; general r=.53 vs .23); the evidence is correlational. Design implication for the agent (not a finding): prefer trace behaviour over self-reported confidence.
agent_test: Compare a stop rule driven by trace features (repeated steps, no new facts) against a rule driven by the model's stated confidence, equal tokens
audit_note: Muncer and Ohtani&Hisasaka verify the online-vs-offline gap (.54 vs .30; .53 vs .23) but it is correlational and 'online' includes think-aloud speech and (in one split) JOL/confidence judgments, so 'what it DOES matters more than what it SAYS' and the agent prescription go beyond the data.
claim_before_audit: The online-vs-offline gap means what a learner DOES while solving (checks, stops, switches) matters more than what it SAYS about itself. For the agent: act on trace behaviour, not on self-reported confidence or style.

claim: Teaching metacognitive or self-regulation strategies raises human achievement (de Boer g=.50 post, .63 follow-up, 48 interventions; Theobald g=.37, 49 studies; Dignath mean .69, 357 effects), but moderators matter: bigger in math, bigger when researchers deliver it.
agent_test: Not directly testable (human training); human effect is trained skill, so do not assume a prompt reproduces it
audit: downgraded 2026-11-01 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Small randomised studies of metacognitive prompts in humans often find no benefit (Engelmann 2021 N=57; Klar 2024 N=201, half ignored prompts). Prompts alone are weaker than trained skill.
agent_test: Check whether the agent actually uses a self-question prompt when given it (compliance), at equal tokens

claim: Swanson (1990) compensation (metacognition offsets low aptitude) is NOT verified: exact N and effect sizes unseen, and the reviewed meta-analyses show moderators of measure type and task complexity, not learner ability.
agent_test: Cannot test on one model; would need weak-vs-strong base model pair under same scaffold

claim: Intrinsic self-review without an external signal does not help and often hurts reasoning: GPT-3.5 CommonSenseQA 75.8 -> 38.1 -> 41.8; GPT-4 GSM8K 95.5 -> 91.5 -> 89.0 over 1, 3, 5 calls. With oracle labels GPT-3.5 GSM8K goes 75.9 -> 84.3 and GPT-4 95.5 -> 97.5. (Gains seen in earlier papers came from oracle stop signals.)
agent_test: Run equal-token arms: no review, always review, review only when an external check fails; expect the last to win
audit_note: Huang et al. Tables 2 and 3 verified (GPT-3.5 CSQA 75.8/38.1/41.8; GPT-4 GSM8K 95.5/91.5/89.0; oracle 75.9->84.3 and 95.5->97.5); the Kamoi survey corroborates; two of the listed Huang entries are the same paper.

claim: A survey finds no demonstrated prompted-LLM self-correction on general tasks; it works with reliable external feedback (code run, search) or after fine-tuning.
schema_part: G / O (review only with external signal)
agent_test: Same arms as K06 on code tasks with unit tests vs math without a checker
audit_note: Kamoi abstract: no prior work shows prompted-LLM self-correction except tasks exceptionally suited to it; works with reliable external feedback; large-scale fine-tuning enables it (claim omits the 'exceptionally suited tasks' exception).

claim: Mistake finding is the bottleneck, not fixing: best GPT-4 step-level mistake finding 52.87% on BIG-Bench Mistake (2,186 traces); backtracking with the true location works well.
agent_test: Give the agent a step-location task; measure localisation accuracy, then fix rate given a true vs its own location, equal tokens

claim: Training can teach intrinsic correction: SCoRe on Gemini lifts MATH self-correction by +15.6 points; base model falls 52.6 -> 41.4 (right-to-wrong 15.8%, wrong-to-right 4.6%) while plain SFT and Self-Refine do not help.
agent_test: Not testable without training; use only as warning that prompting alone will not reproduce it

claim: Models have a self-correction blind spot: 64.5% average over 14 open non-reasoning models fix an error shown as the user's but not the same error in their own output. Appending 'Wait' cut it by 89.3% (mean accuracy +156%).
agent_test: Present own earlier step as 'a colleague's step' vs 'your step' to the agent at equal tokens; test a 'Wait' cue at the review trigger

claim: Reasoning models overthink easy items: o1-like used 1,953% more tokens on '2+3'; in over 92% of cases the first solution round was already right; self-training cut tokens 48.6% on MATH500 with accuracy kept.
agent_test: Add a stop-if-first-answer-checks rule; compare tokens and accuracy with always-continue on easy vs hard items

claim: The opposite failure exists: reasoning models switch strategy too often and abandon promising paths (incorrect answers had more thoughts: e.g. 26.4 vs 12.6 on AIME24 for one model).
agent_test: Log thought-switch counts in agent traces; test a switch-penalty on hard items

claim: Budget forcing with 'Wait' can lift reasoning: s1-32B AIME24 50.0 -> 56.7 (not 57.6, see critique) with 1,000 SFT examples. This is a trained model; gains saturate and limit near the context cap.
agent_test: Test appending a check cue at equal total tokens vs spending those tokens on a second sample (self-consistency)

claim: Skill-labelled routing helps on MATH: +11.6% over CoT, +3.5% over complex CoT, +7.52% over PAL code. It is knowledge of which skill a problem needs, a human-style metacognitive knowledge step.
agent_test: Equal-token test: skill-label then retrieve exemplars vs same tokens as extra CoT samples

claim: Plan-first prompting gives modest zero-shot gains on older models: Plan-and-Solve+ avg 76.7 vs CoT 70.4 across six math sets with text-davinci-003 (GSM8K 59.3 vs 56.4). Self-Discover reports up to +32% over CoT (avg +11% PaLM 2-L, +7% GPT-4).
agent_test: Test plan step on a current strong model; gains likely smaller, so measure at equal tokens
audit_note: Plan-and-Solve Table (CoT 70.4, PS+ 76.7, GSM8K 56.4 vs 59.3) and Self-Discover (up to 32%, BBH avg +11% PaLM 2-L, +7% GPT-4) verified; 'modest' fits PS+ but not Self-Discover's up-to-32%.

claim: Five-stage metacognitive prompting helps NLU by about 3 to 6 points over CoT, small but consistent on GPT-4.
agent_test: Replicate on a current model against CoT with a token-matched CoT-SC arm

claim: Forced Planning-Monitoring-Evaluation structure (Ann Brown prompt) HURTS a standard 8B model on GSM8K (80.71 Std, 77.98 CoT, 69.55 Ann Brown) and does not beat CoT on CorrectBench (75.02 CoT vs 68.14); it is flat on a reasoning-native model (Qwen-3-8B 91.72 vs 91.65).
agent_test: Run ablation: trigger-only metacognitive step vs forced every-step on a weak and strong model

claim: Self-correction funnel (preprint, small counts): of error cases models show awareness 51.2%, correct diagnosis 27.9%, improvement 16.3%; forced structure reached diagnosis 58.3% and improvement 50.0% (12 of 24). Unreplicated.
agent_test: Measure awareness, diagnosis and fix rates separately on the agent's own failed runs

claim: Reflexion gains where a real success signal exists (ALFWorld 130/134 tasks with ReAct+Reflexion; HumanEval pass@1 91.0% vs GPT-4 80.1%, though self-written tests can false-pass and LeetcodeHard was 77.1 vs 80.1); Self-Refine reports about +20% absolute average over seven tasks using only self-feedback, but zero gain on math reasoning (GPT-3.5 64.1 -> 64.1) where the model cannot reliably judge itself (ChatGPT feedback says everything looks good for 94% of instances), with 5%+ gains if an external source flags wrong answers.
agent_test: Test retry-with-reflection only where an external check exists; compare with plain best-of-N at equal tokens
audit_note: Reflexion numbers verified (ALFWorld 130/134, HumanEval 91.0 vs 80.1), Self-Refine +20% avg and math 64.1->64.1 verified, but Self-Refine's gains came from self-feedback without a success signal, so it does not illustrate 'gains when a real success signal exists'; Reflexion was also below GPT-4 on LeetcodeHard (77.1 vs 80.1).
claim_before_audit: Reflexion, Self-Refine and similar loops gain when a real success signal exists (unit tests, environment): ALFWorld 130/134, HumanEval 91% vs 80%; Self-Refine about +20% average but near zero on math where the model must judge itself.

claim: Self-verification by the model itself is unreliable: GPT-4 as its own verifier gives false positives; with a sound external verifier the content of the critique barely matters (about 40% on graph colouring, same as blind resampling n=15).
agent_test: Replace model self-check with a programmatic verifier in one domain; compare against self-check at equal tokens
audit_note: Numbers verified (about 40% with sound verifier, feedback types insignificant, n=15 sampling also 40%; GPT-4 self-verification false positives), but the three listed sources (Stechly 2023, Stechly 2024, Kambhampati 2024) are all from the Kambhampati lab and the position paper adds no data, so it is one lab's evidence; the 40% result is also graph colouring only.

claim: Multi-agent debate does no better than self-consistency at equal compute (GSM8K GPT-3.5: SC 82.5, 85.3, 88.2 at 3, 6, 9 samples).
agent_test: Equal-sample comparison of review loop vs plain majority vote

claim: A small separate meta-controller can cut regulation cost: Meta-R1 used 15.7% to 32.7% of vanilla tokens with accuracy gains (up to +27.3% vs baselines); retrieval version MetaRAG beats Reflexion on HotpotQA (EM 37.8 vs 30.0).
agent_test: Compare a cheap monitor model against self-monitoring at equal total tokens; note benchmarks are authors' own

claim: Multi-agent failures are mostly monitoring failures: 1,600+ traces, 7 frameworks, kappa 0.88; verification 21.3%, misalignment 36.9%, step repetition 15.7%.
agent_test: Add a step-repetition detector to the agent and count how often it fires and whether stopping saves tokens

claim: LLMs are partly calibrated about their own correctness: P(True) and P(IK) work on multiple choice up to 52B; restricting to P(True)>0.5 raises accuracy.
agent_test: Check whether model-stated confidence predicts error on the agent's tasks (calibration curve); use as trigger only if it does

claim: The exact human self-question 'Is it getting me anywhere?' has not been tested head-to-head against stop/switch alternatives in LLMs in the sources read. Gap search 2026-11-01 re-confirmed: six working 2025 triggers all use trace or internal features; none was compared with a prompted self-question.
agent_test: Test the question as the trigger prompt vs trace-feature trigger vs fixed budget at equal tokens

claim: Review without an external signal (intrinsic self-correction) did not help and mostly lowered accuracy on GPT-3.5 and GPT-4, often by turning correct answers into wrong ones (GPT-3.5 CSQA 75.8 -> 38.1 after one round, 41.8 after two; GPT-4 GSM8K 95.5 -> 91.5 -> 89.0 after one and two rounds); the decline is not strictly monotonic in rounds. Kamoi et al. survey: no prior work shows successful self-correction with prompted-LLM feedback outside narrow exceptions. Whether this holds for 2025-26 frontier models was not tested in these sources.
agent_test: Run intrinsic review vs no review vs extra sample at equal tokens on the current backbone
audit_note: Huang Table 3 shows decline is not monotonic with rounds (GPT-3.5 CSQA 75.8->38.1->41.8; GPT-4 CSQA 79.5->80.0; GPT-4 HotpotQA 49.0->49.0 in round 1) and 95.5->89.0 is after 2 self-correction rounds (5 calls), 38.1 is after round 1; the 'no clean token-matched test for 2025-26 frontier models' part is an absence claim neither source addresses.
claim_before_audit: Review without an external signal lowers accuracy on older models and gets worse with more rounds (GPT-3.5 CSQA 75.8 -> 38.1; GPT-4 GSM8K 95.5 -> 89.0 after 3 rounds). No clean token-matched test exists for 2025-26 frontier models.

claim: Where tests or tools exist, review still gains little over equal-budget resampling unless the feedback is good: GPT-4 self-repair 1.05x over pass@20; human feedback raised repair success 33.3% -> 52.6%; CRITIC without the tool falls back near self-consistency.
agent_test: Use tests/tools as review gate; always add an equal-sample arm

claim: Difficulty decides whether sequential revision or parallel resampling wins; an adaptive policy matched best-of-N with about 4x less compute (PaLM 2-S*, MATH).
agent_test: Gate review by an estimated difficulty; compare revise vs resample per difficulty bin

claim: The 'Wait' / other-person framing cue cuts the self-correction blind spot 89.3% on average for non-reasoning open models (Qwen3-14B 0.117 -> 0.868); Sonnet 4 still shows a 41.4% blind spot. Not tested on reasoning models or long agent traces; no length-matched control.
agent_test: Test 'Wait' vs equal-length neutral filler vs 'a colleague wrote this' on the agent's own traces

claim: Overthinking and underthinking need opposite fixes: >92% of first rounds are already correct (stop early), while on hard items wrong answers show many thought switches (switch less; TIP +0.6 to +5.8 Pass@1). No single trigger shown to handle both.
agent_test: Log first-answer-agreement and switch count; test a two-sided rule on easy and hard splits
audit_note: Numbers check out (92%, 1,953%, 48.6%, TIP 38.3->44.1 = +5.8, 83.1->83.7 = +0.6), but the overthinking and underthinking papers are the same Tencent AI Lab group with heavily overlapping authors (Tu, Mi, Yu, Liang, Xu, Song, Chen, He); 'opposite fixes' and 'no single trigger shown' are the researcher's inference, not stated in either paper; Snell is not used for any figure in the claim.

claim: Training-free triggers built from trace or internal signals save tokens at equal or better accuracy: DEER 19.1-80.1% shorter, probe 24% fewer tokens, DeepConf up to 84.7% fewer; shorter-first chains up to 34.5% more accurate than the longest.
agent_test: Implement answer-agreement-at-step-boundary and repeat/switch counters; compare against fixed budget

claim: Meta-R1's separate small monitor gains (14B avg 84.0 -> 87.0, tokens 5,691 -> 3,941) come with no same-model self-monitor arm and no independent replication outside the authors' three benchmarks.
agent_test: Test cheap separate monitor vs same-model monitor at equal total tokens on own tasks

claim: Equal-budget sampling controls erase most of the gain from self-review in code repair and tool-free critique (GPT-4 self-repair reaches at best 1.05x pass@20 on APPS; CRITIC without its tool is near self-consistency), but not for verifier-guided revision, where Snell et al. find sequential revisions beat equal-budget parallel sampling on easy questions and a revision/parallel mix is best on hard ones (up to 4x less compute than best-of-N). Separately, skipping the thinking phase beats full thinking at small budgets (NoThinking 51.3 vs 28.9 on AMC23 at 700 tokens, Ma et al.), which is a thinking control, not a review control. No matched control for metacognitive prompting or Plan-and-Solve on current models was found in these sources.
agent_test: Every S6/prompting test gets an equal-token extra-sample arm
audit_note: Snell et al. show the opposite of 'erase': with a verifier, sequential revisions tend to beat equal-budget parallel sampling (best on easy questions; a mix is best on hard ones; up to 4x compute saving over best-of-N); Ma et al.'s NoThinking 51.3 vs 28.9 (AMC23, 700 tokens) compares skipping thinking to thinking, not a sampling control for a review step; only Olausson (self-repair 1.05x over pass@20 at best) and CRITIC w/o tool near self-consistency support 'erase'.
claim_before_audit: Token-matched sampling controls often erase review gains (self-repair, revision vs best-of-N, NoThinking 51.3 vs 28.9 at 700 tokens). No matched control found for metacognitive prompting or Plan-and-Solve on current models.

claim: Swanson (1990) compensation has still not been read in the original and no replication or prompt-only version was found (search tools out of budget).
agent_test: Read the paper before citing it in the schema rationale
